name: Shackleton rim
evidence: Diviner highland CF ~8.1-8.2 um (Greenhagen 2010); Shackleton on SPA rim, plagioclase-rich (Kaguya)

name: de Gerlache rim
evidence: Diviner highland CF ~8.1-8.2 um; same terrain as Shackleton

name: Haworth rim
lithology: feldspathic highland, some noritic SPA ejecta
evidence: Diviner highland CF; closer to SPA basin (more pyroxene)

name: Faustini rim
lithology: feldspathic highland, some noritic SPA ejecta
evidence: Diviner highland CF; closer to SPA basin (more pyroxene)

name: Mons Mouton summit
evidence: Diviner highland CF; SPA rim massif

name: Shackleton floor (shadow)
evidence: No CF in permanent shadow (no sunlight); same rock as the rim, larger uncertainty (possible frost)

name: Jezero crater (Perseverance)
evidence: TES/THEMIS olivine-rich Nili Fossae region; Perseverance: Seitah olivine cumulate, Maaz basalt

name: Gale crater (Curiosity)
evidence: TES Surface Type 1 nearby; Bagnold dunes olivine basalt (Curiosity)

name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
evidence: Dust-covered in TES (high dust cover index); basaltic plains

name: Gusev crater (Spirit)
evidence: Spirit: Adirondack-class olivine basalt; moderately dusty

name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
evidence: Moderately dusty in TES; basaltic soils (Viking)

name: Utopia Planitia (Viking 2)
evidence: TES Surface Type 2 dominates the northern lowlands (Bandfield 2000; Wyatt & McSween 2002)
